top_story_title: SonicWall SMA1000: maximum-severity flaw exploited days after the patch
top_story_summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-102255, a maximum-severity vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 remote-access appliances. The fix shipped three days before the exploitation report, so the window between patch availability and in-the-wild abuse was measured in days, not weeks. SMA1000 sits at the perimeter and terminates remote-access sessions, which makes it both internet-reachable and a credential-rich target.
top_actions: Inventory every SonicWall SMA1000 appliance, note its running version, and apply the fixed release listed in SonicWall's advisory for CVE-2026-102255 - do not take a build number from press coverage.
Assume compromise on any SMA1000 that was reachable from the internet while unpatched: terminate all active sessions, revoke session tokens, and force re-authentication.
Rotate appliance admin credentials, service-account passwords, certificates and any secrets stored on the appliance after the upgrade.
Hunt the appliance for persistence: unexpected local accounts, modified web resources, new outbound connections, and unusual timestamps in appliance logs.
Pull SMA1000 management and portal access off the public internet where the deployment allows it, and put phishing-resistant MFA plus geo/ASN conditional access on the remote-access portal.
executive_summary: SonicWall SMA1000: CVE-2026-102255, maximum severity, exploited in attacks three days after the patch shipped - the one confirmed-exploitation item this cycle.
Cisco fixed a dozen critical vulnerabilities, five in NX-OS, including unauthenticated root code execution on Nexus switches via a crafted HTTP request to NX-API. Cisco states there is no workaround.

Citrix patched CVE-2026-107406 in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway - a memory overflow reaching RCE or DoS under specific configurations, reported in connection with SAML deployments - and is urging immediate patching.
No KEV additions and no EPSS scores arrived with these items; none of the sources name a fixed build number, so take versions from the vendor advisories only.
Cisco's .conf26 Agentic SOC series describes firewall telemetry feeding an AI triage agent with admin-in-the-loop - worth reading before anyone asks you to give an agent write access to a firewall.
key_actions: **SonicWall** — Check the SonicWall advisory for CVE-2026-102255 for the fixed release and apply it; do not infer a version from news coverage.
**SonicWall** — Terminate all active sessions and revoke session tokens after upgrade - assume stolen session cookies.
**Cisco** — Inventory NX-OS devices and determine which have NX-API enabled; that feature is the attack surface.
**Cisco** — Upgrade NX-OS to the fixed release from Cisco's advisory; validate the ISSU/hitless upgrade path for core and distribution switches first.
**Cisco** — Pull all five advisories from Cisco's security centre and build a single target release that covers every one of them, rather than patching per-CVE.
**Cisco** — Upgrade NX-OS to that fixed release; validate the hitless/ISSU path on distribution switches before touching the core.

**Citrix** — Check each NetScaler ADC and Gateway build against Citrix's advisory for CVE-2026-107406 and apply the hotfix to every unit in the HA pair or device group; verify config sync after the upgrade.
**Citrix** — Identify which virtual servers use SAML authentication and prioritise those appliances.

ai_defenses.solution: Cisco Secure Firewall and Cisco Cloud Control structured Snort 3 and Encrypted Visibility Engine telemetry into Splunk Enterprise Security
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Streams structured Snort 3 and EVE telemetry from Cisco Secure Firewall through Cloud Control into Splunk Enterprise Security, forming the data layer of the .conf26 Agentic SOC pipeline. Cisco describes the model as admin-in-the-loop.
Triages security alerts on Splunk as the SOC data platform, tracked at .conf26 against human-validated workflows rather than running autonomously.

ai_defenses.solution: Cisco Cloud Control with Splunk Enterprise Security (Agentic SOC)
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Cisco reports using Cloud Control and Splunk Enterprise Security to run a live Agentic SOC delivering unified threat detection, investigation and response over .conf26 event traffic.

ai_defenses.solution: Retrospective packet replay with Cisco Secure Firewall, Talos rules and Endace full PCAP
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Replays retained full packet capture against Talos detections published after the traffic occurred, so a zero-day detection can be applied to wire data already on disk.

headlines.title: Max severity SonicWall SMA1000 flaw now exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: A maximum-severity flaw in SonicWall SMA1000 remote-access appliances, CVE-2026-102255, is being exploited three days after the fix shipped.

headlines.title: Cisco NX-OS Software NX-API Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
headlines.summary: Cisco says an unauthenticated attacker can reach root code execution on NX-OS devices through a crafted HTTP request to NX-API, with no workaround available.

headlines.title: Cisco warns of critical flaws allowing Nexus switch takeover
headlines.summary: Five critical NX-OS flaws can give an attacker root-level code execution on Cisco Nexus data centre switches.

headlines.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
headlines.summary: Citrix patched CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that can lead to RCE or DoS in certain SAML configurations.

headlines.title: Cisco Patches a Dozen Critical Vulnerabilities
headlines.summary: Cisco's advisory bundle fixes a dozen critical vulnerabilities spanning unauthorised access, information disclosure, privilege escalation, DoS and remote code execution.

headlines.title: Citrix warns admins to patch new NetScaler RCE flaw immediately
headlines.summary: BleepingComputer reports Citrix telling administrators to patch the new critical NetScaler ADC and Gateway RCE without waiting for a maintenance window.
